subsystems.name: Base garment
subsystems.role: a close-fitting, stretchable shell that carries everything else without restricting movement.
parts: connector hubs at the waist and spine

subsystems.name: Actuator array
subsystems.role: produces touch and pressure sensations at chosen points on the body.
parts: dielectric elastomer or pneumatic bladders for pressure
shape-memory alloy or tendon-driven elements for force cues

subsystems.name: Thermal layer
parts: thermal insulation between pad and skin

subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: measures the wearer's posture and how the suit is being pressed, so feedback can be closed-loop.

subsystems.name: Control electronics
subsystems.role: translates digital commands into drive signals for hundreds of channels.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: supplies peak currents for actuators while staying light enough to wear.

subsystems.name: Software stack
subsystems.role: decides which actuators fire, how hard and when.

buildSteps.title: Map the body and the haptic vocabulary
buildSteps.detail: Decide which sensations matter — contact, vibration, sustained pressure, stretch, temperature — and where they should be felt. Spatial acuity varies hugely: a few millimetres on the fingertips, several centimetres on the back, so actuator spacing follows the body's own resolution.

buildSteps.title: Make the stretchable substrate
buildSteps.detail: Knit or laminate a fabric with conductive yarns, or screen-print stretchable silver or carbon-loaded silicone traces onto an elastic film, then test them through repeated stretching.

buildSteps.title: Build the actuators
buildSteps.detail: Cast thin dielectric elastomer films with compliant electrodes, mould microfluidic bladders and channels, or wind small electromagnetic motors — each chosen for the force, stroke and speed a given body zone needs.

buildSteps.title: Laminate the layers
buildSteps.detail: Stack substrate, actuator layer, thermal pads and sensors, bonding them so the composite still bends with the elbow and knee, and route every trace to a small number of hubs.

buildSteps.title: Wire the electronics
buildSteps.detail: Connect hubs to driver boards, microcontroller and battery, keeping high-voltage actuator lines separated from sensitive sensor lines.

buildSteps.title: Write firmware and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Measure each actuator's response and each wearer's sensitivity, then build per-user lookup tables so a given command feels the same on different bodies.

buildSteps.title: Render haptics in software
buildSteps.detail: Feed physics-engine contacts, distances and temperatures into a mapping layer that decides intensity, timing and spatial pattern, all inside a latency budget of tens of milliseconds.

buildSteps.title: Test and certify safety
buildSteps.detail: Cap skin temperature, pressure and electrical exposure, then run wear trials for comfort, sweat, washing and hundreds of hours of flexing.

prerequisites.why: existing actuators are either strong or fast or light — rarely all three at wearable size and voltage.
wiring must survive thousands of flex cycles and repeated washing without cracking.
haptic realism collapses if feedback arrives after the visual scene has moved on.
hundreds of actuators draw peak currents that a comfortable pack struggles to supply for hours.
without knowing how the skin integrates vibration, pressure and temperature, suits waste actuators on the wrong places.

pathway.milestone: gloves and vests with vibration and limited force feedback in research and niche products
pathway.unlocks: training, teleoperation and immersive entertainment where hands and torso matter most.

pathway.milestone: regional pressure suits with dense actuator arrays and modest temperature control
pathway.unlocks: believable contact with virtual objects across arms, torso and legs.

pathway.milestone: full-body suits with closed-loop sensing and lightweight, multi-hour power
pathway.unlocks: comfortable all-day use, from remote surgery support to rehabilitation.

pathway.milestone: integration with body tracking and, speculatively, direct neural stimulation
pathway.unlocks: sensation that no longer depends on how densely we can pack actuators against the skin.
